question.text: The Account Opening Form (AOF) for clients shall be divided into how many parts, and what does each part contain?

answer.text: Two parts -- Part I captures basic KYC details using CERSAI templates; Part II captures additional intermediary-specific information
Three parts -- KYC, Risk Profile, and Investment Details
One combined form with no separate sections
Four parts -- Identity, Address, Financial Details, and Nominee Details

explanation.text: The Logic: The AOF is divided into two parts. Part I is the KYC portion that captures basic client details using CERSAI KYC templates (with separate templates for individuals and legal entities). Part II captures additional information that is specific to the intermediary's activity. The Trap: The AOF is not three or four parts and is not a single undifferentiated form. The two-part structure keeps the KYC fields uniform across intermediaries (Part I) while allowing each intermediary type to gather what it specifically needs (Part II). Note: The CERSAI templates referenced in Part I are the standard formats prescribed for individual and legal-entity KYC.
